GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  MINUTES
  NOVEMBER 19, 2019

1.  CHAIR SCHMITZ called the meeting to order at 6:32 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT: Schmitz, Zuckerman, Addleman, Arata, Carman,
  Corman, Friedman, Medawar*, Seamans*, Shinn,
  Silvano, Stegura
  * Arrived after minutes approval

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  Bayer, Buresh

  STAFF MEMBERS PRESENT:  Greg Grammer, City Manager
  David Wahba, Director of Community Development
  and Public Works
  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Kelley Thom, Associate Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  ALSO PRESENT:  John Bellas, Principal, Michael Baker International
  Surabhi Barbhaya, Senior Planner, Michael Baker International
  Perry Banner, Senior Planner, Michael Baker International

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  Approval of General Plan Advisory Committee Meeting Minutes, October 15, 2019.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
ADDLEMAN to,

  APPROVE THE GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF
  OCTOBER 15, 2019.

There being no objection, CHAIR SCHMITZ so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

NONE

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  CONSERVATION ELEMENT

Surabhi Barbhaya, Michael Baker International, provided an overview of the topics covered and the
purpose of the Conservation Element. Conservation Elements generally cover conservation and wise
utilization of natural resources. The Conservation Element has a direct relationship with Land Use,
Open Space, and Safety Elements and based on General Plan guidelines they need to correlate.

Ms. Barbhaya continued with a review of the existing policies and stated that some of the policies no
longer apply or have been completed. From the survey that was completed by the GPAC, there was
consensus to either delete them or have them remain as part of the General Plan Update.

Ms. Barbhaya stated, and GPAC concurred, that the following policies have been completed and will
not be included in the Conservation Element:

    Policy 1.7 Provide guidelines for the protection of hillside slopes and canyons, the reduction
  of soil erosion and the control of the velocity of water run-off.

    Policy 1.9 Ensure that the long-term protection of the environment shall be a primary
  consideration in approving development projects. Require all future construction projects, both
  public and private, to mitigate their potential environmental impacts through the environmental
  review process.

General Plan Advisory Committee Meeting  1
Minutes, November 19, 2019
     Policy 1.10 Environmental impact reports for future projects must address cumulative impacts
  which will include other projects on the peninsula, downstream traffic, regional air quality,
  sewage generation and other environmental constraints of the area.

    Policy 1.12 The City will continue to assist the Lead Agency Authority for Chandler Quarry
  pursuant to the State Mining and Reclamation Act (SMARA) requirements related to A.B. 3551
  and A.B. 3903 amendments.

    Policy 3.5 The City will continue to assist the Lead Agency Authority for Chandler Quarry
  pursuant to the State Mining and Reclamation Act requirements related to AB 3551 and AB
  3903 amendment.

    Policy 5.4 Implement criteria for the designation of scenic roadways in the City and evaluate
  existing roadways for their qualities as local scenic routes.

Policy 3.3 (below) will be changed from “Develop” to “Maintain”

    Policy 3.3 Develop Maintain the George F. Canyon open space at Palos Verdes Drive North
  and Palos Verdes Drive East from the water district's pump and extending down the canyon,
  as a cultural and natural preserve. Encourage a cooperative effort to extend the formal
  preservation of George F. Canyon into Rolling Hills and Rancho Palos Verdes Canyon.

From the survey completed by GPAC, there was consensus to keep these policies as part of the
Conservation Element:

    Policy 1.1 Maintain the natural canyons and hillside areas for passive open space and/or for
  incorporation into the Citywide trails system.

    Policy 1.2 Encourage planting of native drought tolerant plant species to minimize erosion and
  to provide habitats for wildlife while being sensitive to the wildfire hazard.

    Policy 1.3 Discourage the excessive grading of slopes in those areas of the City that are
  undeveloped such as canyons, archaeological sites, and areas with established vegetation.

    Policy 2.2 Preserve the existing vegetation in the open space corridors in its natural state while
  being sensitive to fire protection policies.

    Policy 2.3 Encourage the re-establishment of appropriate native plants by requiring
  developments to prepare landscape plans that promote the preservation, protection, and
  enhancement of vegetation, wildlife and natural habitats.

    Policy 2.4 Implement the General Plan guidelines for the restoration of habitats for sensitive
  and/or endangered species.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN asked if there was a place to add a policy, for existing homes,
to encourage replacement of turf with drought tolerant plants.

Ms. Barbhaya stated that there is reference to using less irrigation which in effect translates to
choosing drought tolerant plants.

    Policy 4.1 Cooperate with the South Coast Air Quality Management District (SCAQMD) and
  surrounding cities to develop standards for the enforcement of regulations specific to Rolling
  Hills Estates.

    Policy 4.2 The City will work with the other agencies in the region to ensure that motor vehicles
  comply with all standards for air pollution control.

COMMITTEE MEMBER CARMAN stated that the Environmental Advisory Committee has discussed
the topic of vehicle air pollution.
John Bellas, Michael Baker International stated that Policy 4.2 may be reworded since as it reads, this
is an active policy and may need to be changed to a reactive policy for the city to address violations.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN stated that within policy 4.3, “clear” should be changed to
“clean”.

    Policy 4.3 Implement the clear clean air strategies outlined in the Conservation Element for
  the City to assist in the implementation of the Air Quality Management Plan.

General Plan Advisory Committee Meeting  2
Minutes, November 19, 2019
 COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN stated that there has been discussion on looking into local air
quality monitoring since the current monitoring stations are in Long Beach.

CHAIR SCHMITZ stated that the city does not monitor motor vehicles; she suggested that the policy
should be changed to state that the city is in cooperation with other agencies.

Ms. Barbhaya suggested that the following policies be combined to create one new policy.

    Policy 5.1 Encourage the preservation of view corridors and discourage developments and
  additions which obstruct view corridors.

    Policy 5.2 Implement the General Plan criteria for the designation of scenic roadways, with
  consideration for the visibility of scenery, major landform, vegetation, structures, and
  panoramas, and develop a plan for the undergrounding of existing telephone and electrical
  poles.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ADDLEMAN stated that there should be mention of prohibiting the widening
of Palos Verdes Drive North. Mr. Bellas stated that this could be addressed when the Transportation
Element is discussed.

COMMITTEE MEMBER CORMAN asked if undergrounding of existing utilities is only for the scenic
roadways or is it a plan for the City in general. Ms. Barbhaya stated that this is only restricted for the
scenic roadways. A discussion ensued on the feasibility of doing this on a wider scale.

The following policy will remain with the following changes:

    Policy 5.2 Implement the General Plan criteria for the designation of scenic roadways with
  consideration for the visibility of scenery, major landform, vegetation, structures, and
  panoramas, and develop a plan for the undergrounding of existing telephone and electrical
  poles.

Mr. Bellas suggested adding a new policy which includes undergrounding utilities for the prevention
of wildfires caused by electrical wires.

    Policy 5.3 Preserve the existing rural road character roadway geometry of Palos Verdes Drive
  North by maintaining the roadway's designation as a scenic corridor/roadway part of a
  peninsula wide loop.

A discussion ensued on adding other City roadways, which include, Rolling Hills Road, Palos Verdes
Drive East and Silver Spur Road.

COMMITTEE MEMBER SEAMANS inquired about Hawthorne Blvd. and Crenshaw Blvd. and
expressed concerns with future need to plan for getting people off the Peninsula in case of an
emergency.

Director Wahba noted a correction to the map which shows Crenshaw from Silver Spur to Indian Peak
in the city and this should be revised since it is now part of Rancho Palos Verdes.

Mr. Bellas added that the roadways are important and scenic for various reasons and it would be
helpful for future staff to understand why the roadways are designated as scenic.

The following policy will remain:

    Policy 5.6 Continue to promote the rural environment of the City by discouraging light and
  glare except where lighting is required for public safety.

The following policy will remain with the following changes:

    Policy 6.1 Evaluate and distinguish between the destruction of land and the enhancement of
  land. Discourage any grading beyond that necessary to create adequate building pads and
  reasonable recreation areas for equestrian use, pools, tennis courts, etc.

COMMITTEE MEMBER FRIEDMAN stated that Policy 6.2 (below) should be moved to Land Use and
the GPAC agreed.

General Plan Advisory Committee Meeting  3
Minutes, November 19, 2019
     Policy 6.2 The project review process must give major consideration to the health, safety, and
  welfare of the community without violating the homeowners' rights to modify/improve their
  property. (Move to Land Use Element)

The following policies will remain with the following changes:

    Policy 6.3 Preserve natural land forms, vegetation, and wildlife and discourage by requiring
  more stringent regulations for the development and alteration of slopes greater than 2 to 1.

    Policy 1.5 Develop and implement update a comprehensive program for the recycling of waste
  such as paper, aluminum, bottles, organic waste, and motor oil pursuant with the requirements
  of AB939, AB1820, and AB2707. City Manager Grammer stated that electronic waste and
  household hazardous waste needs to be added.

The following policy will move to the Land Use Element:

    Policy 1.11 The City planning staff will strengthen enforcement of planning ordinances and
  standards, including those regulations concerning the maintenance of private property. (Move
  to Land Use Element)

The following policy will be removed:

    Policy 2.1 Strive to protect the remaining wildlife population of the area and prevent the
  destruction of the remaining natural habitats.

The following policy will remain with the following changes:

    Policy 3.1 Continue to implement Implement the General Plan guidelines for the protection of
  sites of paleontological, archaeological, historical or culturally valuable significance.
  Recognize the importance of these resources and continue to regulate them through the
  zoning.

The following policy will remain:

    Policy 3.2 Encourage and support local high quality projects and programs devoted to the
  visual and performing arts, the sciences, the humanities, and educational programs related to
  these topics.

The following policy will remain with the following changes:

    Policy 3.4 Explore funding for a nature/environmental center for the City, possibly to be
  connected with the George F. Canyon open space/natural preserve. Work with the City of
  Rolling Hills to promote the preservation of the canyon areas within its corporate boundaries.

COMMITTEE MEMBER CARMAN inquired about the opportunity to include a policy regarding the
Metropolitan Water District (MWD) site (south east corner of Palos Verdes Drive North / Palos Verdes
Drive East). Director Wahba stated that a policy could be created that speaks on enhancing the
property. Mr. Bellas agreed and stated, the policy could speak on enhancement, not enforcement,
since it is not city property. Mr. Bellas stated that MBI staff will work on this.
The following policy will remain:

    Policy 5.5 Implement criteria and procedures for the preservation and beautification of present
  and future roadways and for the designated scenic roadways.

Ms. Barbhaya presented new policies for discussion.

The following policy is similar to a previous policy and therefore, is not necessary:

    Identify priority areas to conserve that offer the most effective and efficient protection of the
  natural resource systems.

The following policy will be included in the Conservation Element:

    Encourage the use of high efficiency irrigation technology, and recycled site water to reduce
  the use of potable water for irrigation.

The following policy will be included in the Conservation Element with the following changes:

General Plan Advisory Committee Meeting  4
Minutes, November 19, 2019
     Encourage use of native plant species, drought tolerant plants and xeriscaping for landscaping
  and restrict use of landscaping that require high levels of irrigation.

CHAIR SCHMITZ stated that the Pepper Tree is not a native tree and would like to discuss considering
other tree species when replanting.

Mr. Bellas stated that a policy could be formulated to consider an Urban Forestry program that looks
at changing the tree species in the community.

The following policy will be included in the Conservation Element with the following changes:

    Remove, avoid, or discourage the planting and support programs that remove of invasive plant
  species.

The following policy will be included in the Conservation Element with the changes as noted:

    Encourage low impact development for storm water management and encourage innovative
  techniques. such as,
  · Bioretention basins, bio swales, and rain gardens designed to capture and soak in
  stormwater
  · Reduction of impervious surfaces and use of permeable paving
  · Rain barrel/ rainwater harvesting
  · Green roof

The following policy will not be included in the Conservation Element:

    Expand the Energy Efficiency Climate Action Plan (2015) to include water conservation, waste
  reduction, land use, and alternative modes of transportation.

The following policy will be discussed as part of the Sustainability Element:

    Eliminate use of single use plastic and polystyrene disposable products in the restaurant and
  food service industry.

The following policy will be included in the Conservation Element with the following changes:

    Develop a manure best management practices program that includes guidelines for storage
  and composting of manure.

The following policy will be included in the Conservation Element:

    Create Urban Forestry program to maintain a resilient and healthy tree canopy in the City.

The following policy will be included in the Conservation Element with the following changes:

    Develop and implement Support public education programs related to site development and
  conservation of resources.

The following policy will be discussed as part of the Sustainability Element:

    Seek funding to incorporate renewable energy alternatives in public buildings.

The following policy will be included in the Conservation Element with the following changes:

    Encourage Ensure site planning that conserves natural resources continuing to implement the
  municipal code requirements, including: natural land forms, view sheds, etc.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MEDAWAR stated that the policy (below) should consider lighting that is
needed for the safety of the commercial district and be sensitive to the neighboring residential homes.

COMMITTEE MEMBER SEAMANS stated that Chandler Ranch Road is dark and stated that for safety
reasons there should be adequate lighting.

The following policies (below) have been addressed within a previously reviewed policy:

General Plan Advisory Committee Meeting  5
Minutes, November 19, 2019
     Restrict/ control outdoor light and glare from development projects to retain the quality of night
  skies by minimizing light pollution.

    Minimize obtrusive light by limiting outdoor lighting that is misdirected, excessive, or
  unnecessary.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN recommended to include a policy on limiting the number of
utility vaults.

    Require new development to place utilities underground unless infeasible and encourage
  “undergrounding” in existing development to maintain viewsheds, reduce hazards associated
  with hanging lines and utility poles.

The following policy will be included in the Conservation Element:

    Work with Palos Verdes Peninsula Land Conservancy to maintain the existing land preserved
  for conservation and identify land for additional land conservation

The following policy will not be included in the Conservation Element:

    Support Countywide stormwater quality programs.

The following policy will be included in the Conservation Element:

    Revisit the Scenic Corridor Overlay Zone and establish guidelines for development along these
  corridors to preserve the character and viewsheds.

B.  OPEN SPACE AND RECREATION ELEMENT

This item will be discussed at the next GPAC meeting.

6.  COMMITTEE ITEMS

NONE

7.  CONSULTANT/STAFF ITEMS

Planning Manager Naughton stated that the City of Rolling Hills Estates and the City of Rancho Palos
Verdes are preparing a Hazard Mitigation Plan. Per the Disaster and Mitigation Act, it is required that
it is updated every five years. Planning Manager Naughton encouraged GPAC members to review
and provide comments on the draft Hazard Mitigation Plan, which is available on the City’s website
through December 11, 2019. The Hazard Mitigation Plan will be incorporated into the Safety Element.

8.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR SCHMITZ adjourned the meeting at 8:38 p.m. The next General Plan Advisory Committee
meeting will be held on Tuesday, December 17, 2019.

General Plan Advisory Committee Meeting  6
Minutes, November 19, 2019
